mean: a husband, the man of a hearth
a wife, the woman of a hearth
a grandmother, an old mother of the hearth
a friend, one who stands beside
a foe, one who comes against
a lord, one who holds land
a trader, one who carries goods
one who keeps the rolls, a clerk
one who shuts in, a gaoler
one who knows the water, a ship-master
a worker of wood, a boatwright
a youth, one not yet grown
one bereft: an orphan, a widow
a troop, a band under one leader
a council, those who sit and weigh
a fever, a burning of the body
the middle of the day, noon
a week, a turn of days
a bay, a bend of the shore
a rib of a hull or a body
a strake, a line of planking
a vault, an arched room below
a gallery, a way cut in rock
a window, an eye in a wall
a niche, a small hollow in a wall
a ruin, a thing broken down
a volley, a shower of shot
a rite, a thing done in order
prune, cut back to help grow
